accepted.title: Gross–Siebert reconstruction of higher-dimensional projective-space Batyrev mirrors
accepted.text: Let k be algebraically closed of characteristic0 and n≥4. Consider the Batyrev degeneration {t f_{n+1}(x₀,…,x_n)+∏_{i=0}^n x_i=0}⊂ℙⁿ×Spec k[[t]], where f_{n+1} is a general homogeneous polynomial of degree n+1, polarized by the anticanonical class. Use its Gross–Siebert dual intersection complex B=∂Conv(e₁,…,e_n,−e₁−⋯−e_n), with the induced integral affine structure. On each adapted slab use the normalized initial function 1+∑_{j=3}^n z^{(n+1)ē_j}, where ē₃,…,ē_n form the slab tangent-lattice basis, with the monodromy transition rules. Can the Gross–Siebert reconstruction algorithm be performed with natural compatible choices despite the failure of local rigidity, producing a toric degeneration mirror in ℙⁿ of the form {η(t)∑_{i=0}^n ϑ_i^{n+1}+∏_{i=0}^nϑ_i=0}, for some η(t)∈k[[t]], and a rational map to the dual Batyrev degeneration in the toric variety of the polar polytope, given by x_i↦ϑ_i in Cox coordinates?
